Why Humour (as 'tis ens ) we thus define it To be a quality of aire or water, And in it selfe holds these two properties, Moisture and fluxure: As, for demonstration, Powre water on this floore, 'twill wet and runne: Likewise the aire (forc't through a horne or trumpet) Flowes instantly away, and leaues behind A kind of dew; and hence we doe conclude, That what soe're hath fluxure, and humiditie, As wanting power to containe it selfe, Is Humour: so in euery humane body The choller, melancholy, flegme, and bloud, By reason that they flow continually In some one part, and are not continent, Receiue the name of Humours.
